analysis.summary:
This 34-year-old male presents with stress-triggered patchy hair loss occurring in the context of significant work-related emotional stress. All Four Examinations findings converge on a clear diagnosis of Liver Qi Stagnation Transforming into Heat with underlying Liver Yin Deficiency. The wiry and slippery pulse is the pathognomonic finding for Liver Qi stagnation with heat transformation; the wiry quality is definitive for Liver pattern in classical texts, while the slippery component indicates heat transformation and some Yin insufficiency. The weak and sunken rear pulse position indicates Kidney Yin deficiency at a constitutional level, explaining the patient's tendency toward Yin-deficiency patterns. The red tongue body directly confirms internal heat presence. The thin yellow coating is critical: the thin coat specifically indicates Yin deficiency (Yin provides the fluids that generate coating thickness), while yellow indicates heat. Purple stasis at the tongue edges reflects Blood stagnation secondary to heat transformation.

Clinical presentation perfectly integrates with this pattern differentiation. The rage and irritability after months of work stress represent classic Liver Qi stagnation emotional manifestation—the Liver governs the free coursing of Qi, and when emotions are constrained (inability to express work frustration), Liver Qi becomes stuck and develops into rage outbursts. Facial redness, thirst, and hot flashes represent direct internal heat manifestations. The insomnia with sleep under six hours reflects Heart Yin deficiency secondary to Liver heat disrupting Heart function. The Heart houses Consciousness; when Heart Yin fails to provide cooling stability, sleep becomes impossible.

Alopecia areata, an autoimmune-mediated condition, develops when internal heat damages hair root tissue combined with Liver Blood and Yin deficiency failing to nourish hair growth. The clear stress trigger and constitutional Qi-stagnant presentation indicates that emotional constraint is the primary driver. Excessive sweating reflects both heat consuming fluids and Yin deficiency's inability to secure the boundary between Wei Qi and nutritive circulation (which prevents excessive sweating). The tight abdomen with chest and rib-side fullness is the classic Liver Qi stagnation location signature in TCM anatomy.

Treatment must address three integrated levels: course the Liver and move stagnant Qi to restore normal Liver function, clear the internal heat developed from prolonged stagnation, and supplement Liver and Heart Yin to address underlying deficiency and prevent recurrence. Critical to success is lifestyle modification addressing the primary emotional cause, particularly stress management and emotional expression practices. The prognosis is favorable—Liver Qi patterns respond well to coursing treatment, and with stress reduction, improvements typically manifest within 2-3 months. Hair regrowth may require 3-6 months given the immune nature of alopecia areata, but progression toward healing should become evident within 8-12 weeks.

recommendations.emotional_care: The Liver system is the most emotionally sensitive organ system in classical medicine; this patient's condition has an emotional root cause and will not resolve without addressing emotional patterns. Implement daily emotional processing through: (1) Journaling for 10-15 minutes daily, specifically externalizing work frustrations rather than internalizing them—write out complaints, grievances, and unexpressed thoughts to prevent Qi constraint; (2) Practice assertiveness and boundary-setting at work by rehearsing how to voice concerns before they accumulate; (3) Engage in activities purely for enjoyment unrelated to work 3-4 times weekly through reading, hobbies, time with friends to build emotional resilience; (4) Consider therapy or counseling if work stress is unresolvable or ongoing; (5) Practice 4-7-8 breathing (inhale for 4 counts, hold for 7 counts, exhale for 8 counts) multiple times daily to interrupt rage reactivity before escalation; (6) Practice daily loving-kindness meditation or forgiveness meditation (5-10 minutes) to prevent resentment from chronically damaging Liver function. precautions.special_notes: Alopecia areata is an autoimmune condition that responds well to classical medicine Liver coursing and heat-clearing treatment, but conventional dermatology evaluation is still recommended to rule out nutritional deficiencies such as iron, B12, and zinc; thyroid dysfunction such as hyperthyroidism which can cause similar heat signs and hair loss; and other medical causes. Ensure baseline thyroid panel and micronutrient testing through primary care if not already done. The work stress trigger is clear and primary, but autoimmune alopecia can have multifactorial causes. This treatment addresses the Liver-emotional component which is currently driving the pattern; this will likely benefit the hair loss significantly but integrated care with dermatology for direct hair support through topical treatments and nutritional support may accelerate recovery. Hair regrowth typically requires minimum 3-6 months even with optimal treatment, so patience and consistency are essential. Premature discontinuation of treatment is a common cause of failure—commit to minimum 3-month course before assessing efficacy.

follow_up.timeline: First follow-up assessment at 2-3 weeks to evaluate initial response to acupuncture and herbal treatment. Main reassessment at 6-8 weeks to confirm pattern differentiation and adjust formula if needed. Ongoing monthly monitoring for 3-6 months to track hair regrowth progression and ensure lifestyle modifications are sustainable.
follow_up.expected_improvement: First 2-3 weeks: noticeable reduction in rage and irritability (typically the most rapid response), improvement in sleep duration moving from below 6 hours toward 7-8 hours, some anxiety relief, softening of chest tightness. At 4-6 weeks: facial redness begins to diminish visibly, thirst decreasing, excessive sweating normalizing, pulse palpably becoming less wiry and rapid. At 8-12 weeks: first visible signs of hair regrowth in affected patches appearing as small hair nubs, overall sense of wellbeing markedly improved, energy levels increased, emotional reactivity significantly reduced, heat signs largely resolved. At 12+ weeks with continued treatment: sustained and progressive hair regrowth, complete resolution of acute heat signs, durable emotional stability even under work stress, improved constitutional baseline health.
follow_up.next_steps: First: Schedule initial acupuncture treatment with qualified TCM acupuncturist experienced in pattern-based treatment, ideally weekly or twice-weekly for first 4 weeks. Second: Begin herbal formula treatment immediately (can run concurrent with acupuncture—they are synergistic). Third: Implement lifestyle modifications starting immediately including 7-8 hour sleep schedule, daily stress management practice (meditation and journaling), and Tai Chi or Qigong practice. Fourth: Schedule dermatology evaluation if not already done to assess autoimmune status, thyroid function, and micronutrient levels (iron, B12, zinc). Fifth: Return at 2-3 weeks with practitioner with update on sleep quality, mood changes, chest tightness, and any visible pulse or tongue changes to confirm pattern diagnosis and track progress. Sixth: If not seeing improvement in sleep or irritability by week 3, consider short-term pharmacological sleep support from physician while other treatments build their effects. Seventh: At 6-8 week reassessment, if hair regrowth not yet visible but other signs improved, continue same formula; if worsening or no improvement in core symptoms by week 6, obtain pulse and tongue reassessment to confirm pattern or identify need for formula modification.
